problem_markdown: Subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_{2n+1}$ of $B$ each contain $2n$ elements, every pair intersects in exactly one element, and every element of $B$ lies in at least two subsets. For which $n$ can the elements be labelled zero or one with exactly $n$ zeros in each $A_i$?
solutions_markdown:
Fix $A_i$. Its $2n$ elements must each belong to another subset, while the $2n$ other subsets each intersect it only once. Thus every element belongs to exactly two subsets, and there is one element for every pair $\{i,j\}$. Regard that element as an edge of the complete graph on $2n+1$ vertices.

Zero-labelled edges would form a graph of degree $n$ at every vertex. Its degree sum $n(2n+1)$ must be even, forcing $n$ even.

Conversely suppose $n$ is even. Number the vertices modulo $2n+1$ and label an edge zero precisely when its cyclic difference is one of $\pm1,\ldots,\pm n/2$. Each vertex then meets exactly $n$ zero edges; label the rest one. Therefore precisely the positive even integers $n$ work.
